text:
Priya: Quick flag  noticed a cluster of WS reconnects starting 2026-04-05T03:14Z. Console shows many of them as client_timeout rather than routing_handoff. Anyone else seeing misclassification? :thinking:

kevin: I pulled some traces from edge-proxy. The proxy returned 204 then a routing change within 80ms. Clients interpret 204 as terminal and retry, which ends up as a new session.

Lena: That 204 on keepalive is intended as a soft acknowledgement in our proxy path, but if routing decides to move the session mid-ack it looks like a different slab_id on resume. We should probably avoid 204 when slab is in a transition state.

ara: The slab manager marks targets `draining=true` and we currently let TCP/socket linger for a bit. But the keepalive code path uses `soft_close` which maps to 204 for HTTP SSE and a normal close for WS. We should make the keepalive response include a header `X-Routing-State: transitioning` so the client lib can treat it as retryable-with-resume.

Sam: Metering shows ~2.1k duplicate session charges in the 10m window. Billing metadata is looking at conn_start events only; we need to cross-reference resume tokens to avoid double charging for quick restarts.

Priya: Sample log (sanitized):

```
2026-04-05T03:14:21.112Z route=outbound slab=slab-a session=xyz conn_status=204 keepalive=true
2026-04-05T03:14:21.190Z route=outbound slab=slab-b resume_attempt=1 resume_ok=false reason="session_mismatch"
```

kevin: That's the exact signature. If the slab swap happens between those two events the client sees resume_ok=false and opens a new connection.

Lena: UX ask for Console: show "active rollout metadata" on the reconnect alert (canary%, draining slabs, slab-manager-change-id). Right now alerts only show error class and sample logs which makes it hard to triage if it was rollout-related.

ara: On the proxy side I'll add `X-Routing-State` and emit `routing_transition=true` in structured logs when a slab is flagged draining and we still respond to keepalive. Also set `handoff_hint=planned` for planned rollouts.

Sam: Ops-bot: created incident INC-2026-331 to track duplicates and billing impact.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-331 created; severity P3.

Priya: We also need a short-lived billing mitigation: treat reconnections within 1s that present the same resume_id as continuation (not new session) for metering. Make it opt-in per account.

kevin: Note: client libs vary. Some drop resume tokens on first 204. DevEx we should publish a tiny note to recommend honoring `X-Routing-State` and keeping resume_id across soft closes.

Lena: I'll add a console panel `reconnect_by_routing_state` that correlates `routing_transition` logs with `conn_status` and `resume_ok` to make it easy to spot rollout-induced churn.

ara: PR #712 will add header and log flag. Will include unit tests and backcompat toggle (env var) so we can flip quickly.

Sam: I'll prototype the 1s metering grace and run it against a replay of the 10m window to ensure we don't under-bill.

Priya: Action items recap: 1) @ara add header + log flag PR, 2) @Lena dashboard + panel, 3) @Sam meter-grace prototype, 4) @kevin coordinate client-lib note with DevEx, 5) DevEx update rollout playbook to include rollback threshold for reconnect rate.

kevin: One more: can we emit `slab_change_id` in logs so we can pivot on exact manager commit that caused the handoff? Makes postmortems much cleaner.

ara: Good call. I'll include `slab_change_id` in that PR. ETA 45m.

Priya: Thanks. If reconnects spike again I'll flip the canary and ping oncall.
